summary: Announces that the Haskins Laboratory Very Distant Host connection would move from BBN's IMP to Harvard's IMP, changing the Host's network address from 197 to 201 while its host number stayed the same.

eli5.summary: A lab's computer was moving to a different network box, so its address changed. This warns people to update.

subtitle: Haskins Lab's network address moves from 197 to 201

tldr.problem: A research facility's host computer needs to move from BBN's network connection to Harvard's, requiring a network address change.
tldr.mechanism: The very distant host connection is physically moved from BBN IMP number 5 to Harvard IMP number 9, while the host number stays the same at 3.
tldr.outcome: The network address changes from 197 to 201 to reflect the new IMP connection, and users must update their routing information.

today: RFC 634 is an infrastructure notice from the early ARPANET. The address change it announces is historical and has no relevance to modern networks.

sections.title: Address Change Notice
sections.content:
RFC 634 announces that the Haskins Laboratory Very Distant Host connection will move between telephone company circuits managed by different network facilities. The host was attached to BBN (the Boston node, IMP #5) and will move to Harvard (IMP #9). The host number—the identifier within that facility—remains 3, but the overall network address changes from 197 to 201 to reflect the new connection point.

The move depends on the local telephone company completing new circuits, so the exact date is uncertain but expected between May 8 and May 22, 1974. Users and network operators will need to update their address tables to route messages to the new location.
sections.eli5: A computer is moving to a different box on the network, so its address number changes. The notice says which computers need to know the new address.

sections.title: Network Address Scheme
sections.content:
In the ARPANET, network addresses are assigned based on the IMP (Interface Message Processor) serving the host and the host position within that IMP. The address 197 identified the Haskins Lab host on IMP #5 (BBN), and address 201 identifies the same host on IMP #9 (Harvard). The host number—position 3—is preserved because it remains the same logical resource; only its attachment point changes.

This scheme requires all network nodes to maintain current address tables so that routing decisions correctly locate hosts when they move between IMP connections. The RFC is thus not only an announcement but also an operational requirement: administrators must update their network configuration.
sections.eli5: The address is a combination of which network box and which position in that box. When the computer moves to a different box, both parts of the address change even though it's the same computer.

sections.title: Historic Notice
sections.content: RFC 634 is an infrastructure notice from the earliest days of ARPANET. It documents the administrative process for managing host migrations on the network. The specific address change announced is historical and has no modern relevance, but the RFC demonstrates how early networks required explicit coordination and communication about topology changes.
sections.eli5: This is just a note from 1974 telling other computers about a move. It does not affect anything today.
